value.course_overview: Develop the advanced training in the skills required to address interconnected environmental challenges through the application of science, technology, economics, policy, innovation, and systems thinking. You will learn from leading researchers and practitioners, and study alongside students from diverse backgrounds to explore how environmental change interacts with society, policy and innovation. You will have the opportunity to meet and learn from experts and industry professionals, helping you develop the critical evaluation skills, research techniques and methods essential for a career in sustainability. You can specialise through elective modules and by focusing your dissertation on your own interests and career goals. Choices include Biodiversity, Business, Climate, Economics, Energy, Entrepreneurship, Policy, Pollution, Water, Waste, Urban Transitions, and more. You’ll graduate from a world-leading university, with in-demand skills and knowledge that prepares you for many future career paths in sustainability, including business, consulting, finance, policymaking and research. Delivered by Imperial’s Centre for Environmental Policy, the MSc Sustainability, Environmental Policy and Innovation is the new name for Imperial's MSc in Environmental Technology, building on 50 years of cutting-edge sustainability teaching and research with an alumni network of over 6000 successful graduates and sustainability professionals worldwide.

Spring term / Learning pathways: Pathway 1: Policy, Innovation and Sustainable Futures
Pathway 3: Energy Policy and Systems Innovation
Spring term / Special topic modules: Climate Impacts and Adaptation across the world
Citizen Science - Innovation, Theory, Policy & Practice

selection_and_structure_instructions: In term one you will study modules that build your understanding of environmental systems, sustainability challenges, and innovation. In addition to the two core modules, you will also select a special topic module, which will allow you to tailor the course to your interests and engage with emerging sustainability topics. Please note that the list of optional ,special topic modules (electives) is subject to change.

In the second term you begin to specialise by choosing a learning pathway that aligns with your interests. Each pathway provides a choice of modules allowing you to tailor the course to your career goals. In addition to your two chosen pathway modules, you will also choose a special topic module. Please note that the list of optional, special topic modules (electives) is subject to change.
Apply your learning to explore a sustainability problem of your choice in-depth, with academic supervision.

The project can be desk and/or laboratory-based and/or involve fieldwork and can be carried out in conjunction with an outside organisation.

value.course_overview: Transform the future of farming and tackle the biggest challenges in food production and ecosystem health, with our MSc designed for aspiring agricultural scientists, technologists, and sustainability professionals. Explore how ecological principles and cutting-edge technologies can be applied to create more resilient, productive, and sustainable farming systems. Dive into topics like biological control, integrated crop management, agritech innovation, and sustainable livestock production. You’ll gain hands-on experience through fieldwork, lab sessions, and exclusive visits to agritech companies, research farms, and commercial operations. You’ll also build essential research skills in use of R, statistics and data science – tools that are increasingly vital in modern agriculture. A major highlight of the programme is your five-month independent research project, where you’ll choose a topic that inspires you and develop your own research. You’ll have the opportunity to collaborate with external partners or undertake a placement, and your work will culminate in a thesis and presentation. Whether you’re looking to innovate in the agritech sector, influence agricultural policy, or contribute to global food security, this course gives you the knowledge, experience, and confidence to make a real impact. Living Planet courses at Silwood Park This course is part of the "Living Planet" family of courses based at Silwood Park. MSc Biodiversity, Carbon and Nature-Based Solutions MSc Computational Ecology and Evolution MRes Ecology, Evolution and Conservation MRes Ecology, Evolution and Conservation with AI Methods MSc Ecology, Evolution and Conservation MSc Ecology, Evolution and Conservation with AI Methods MSc Sustainable Agriculture and Technology (this course) We can discuss which course is the best fit to you at the interview stage of your application. It is normally possible to transfer to a different living planet course at that stage if you wish.

Core modules: Silwood Field Programme and Basic Computing

project_and_pathway_conditions: Research project Take the lead in your own research.
You'll receive extensive training in research skills on an extended five-month independent research project.
Working closely with a supervisor, you’ll have the opportunity to conduct your project in the lab, field, or through computational analysis – often based at Silwood Park.
Your project will culminate in a written thesis and a research presentation, giving you the chance to apply scientific methods to real-world agricultural challenges and showcase your expertise.

value.course_overview: Synthetic Cell Science is an emerging field at the intersection of physical, life, and engineering sciences. This course will equip you with the skills to build synthetic cells – biomimetic nano‑ and micro‑robots assembled from non‑living components that replicate real cellular behaviours such as metabolism, communication, decision‑making, motility, and even evolution. You will learn to create biodevices ranging from biological circuits to organelles, cells, and tissues, and explore how synthetic cells can revolutionise both fundamental research and applications across therapeutics, agrochemical delivery, diagnostics, regenerative medicine, green biosynthesis, and bioremediation. Through hands‑on experience you will design, build, and characterise synthetic cells using microfluidics, 3D bioprinting, AI, microscopy, membrane engineering, and other technologies. You will work in world‑class facilities, such as the £200M Molecular Sciences Research Hub and the £5M Advanced Hackspace, and apply your designs to translational challenges, such as delivery in biological systems. You will develop close links with industry and NGOs, gaining expertise required for further study at PhD level or for a career in industry and the SME sector, where synthetic cell skills are in high demand. The course begins with a lecture series led by world‑leading experts, covering the fundamentals of synthetic cell science. You will then undertake a hands‑on training project (HackSynCell), followed by a nine‑month independent, original, interdisciplinary research project in Synthetic Cell Science. By the end of the course, you will be ready to lead the next wave of synthetic cell innovation from fundamental discovery to impactful application.

value.course_overview: This advanced graduate programme will provide you with the knowledge and skills needed for a career in the modern transport sector. Understand the causes and motivations behind the movement of people and goods across the wide range of available modes of transport. Become part of a global community of thousands of graduates who have embarked on their transport careers after completing our postgraduate courses. Discover the techniques used to analyse transport problems before exploring the policies and measures required to resolve such problems. You will learn to evaluate transport projects and policies, considering the political, social, environment, commercial and financial issues involved. Our programme is a career-orientated and will cover theoretical background, practical design, and analysis considerations central to the concepts of efficiency, safety, security, and sustainability. This course will equip you for further PhD research in this specialist area or a future career in transport planning, engineering, operations, management or policy. Choosing your stream You have the option of choosing between two streams. You should consider which stream is right for you according to your career aims and background. If an offer of admission is made, it will correspond to a specific stream. Switching streams is not possible once you have commenced your studies. value.career_outcomes: How will studying at Imperial help my career? Learn from an insider's perspective and gain a wealth of industry knowledge to help you succeed in your career as a climate change expert. Through a partnership with Grantham Institute, we enhance our excellent reputation as a provider of sustainable business education. With its Climate Leadership Award, the programme has been recognized for its innovative approach to addressing the climate crisis. With specialised knowledge, you'll be highly sought after in a range of sectors. Finance, consulting, and CleanTech are just some of your options. Other potential career paths include education and energy.

Choosing your stream - Clinical Research Consider which Clinical Research stream is right for you, according to your career aims and research interests. When applying via our application portal My Imperial, at the start of the process you should choose the relevant mode and level of study: MRes 1YFT (1 year full-time) or MRes 2YPT (2 years part-time). Then, you will choose your specialist stream, later in the application platform. If an offer of admission is made, it will correspond to a specific stream. Switching streams is only possible under certain conditions.
value.career_outcomes: How will studying at Imperial help my career? Graduates of our faculty of medicine courses go on to succeed in a wide range of sectors. These include healthcare, pharmaceuticals, government, charities and NGOs, consultancy, technology, research and development, education. Who do our graduates work for? Our faculty of medicine graduates have worked for companies including Cancer Research, NHS, Department of Health and Social Care, Costello Medical, Medpace, Sanofi, AstraZenica, Oxford Genetics, Wellcome Stranger Institute. What jobs do our graduates do? Data analyst, Policy advisor, Trainee Patent Attorney, Project Manager, Medical Affairs Writer, Associate Scientist, Regulatory advisor, Healthcare Consultant. What about further study? PhD at leading institutions worldwide. What careers support does Imperial offer? Our Careers Service can support you as you consider your next steps. You can access one-to-one guidance, workshops, employer events and online resources to help you explore y

value.application_fee_terms: Application fee If you are applying for a Master’s course, you will need to pay an application fee before submitting your application. The fee applies per application and not per course. The application fees for postgraduate courses are: £90 for all Master's applications, excluding those to Imperial Business School £125 for MSc applications to Imperial Business School £150 for MBA applications to Imperial Business School There is no application fee for Postgraduate Certificates, Postgraduate Diplomas, or courses such as PhDs and EngDs. This includes MRes and PhD combined (1+3) courses with the Centre for Doctoral Training. If you are facing financial hardship and are unable to pay the application fee, we encourage you to apply for our application fee waiver. Read full details about the application fee and waiver . Choosing your stream Consider which stream is right for you, according to your career aims, research interests, and the entry requirements. If you hold an MBBS degree (or international equivalent), you are encouraged to apply for the Clinical Robotics & AI stream. If you do not hold an MBBS degree (or international equivalent), please apply for the core Medical Robotics & Image-Guided Intervention stream. You should apply for your chosen stream at the start of the application process in our application portal My Imperial. Look for the exact stream name in the list of courses: Medical Robotics and Image Guided Intervention (MRes 1YFT) Medical Robotics and Image Guided Intervention (Clinical Robotics and AI) (MRes 1YFT)

Selection Assessing your application Admissions Tutors consider all the evidence available during our rigorous selection process and the College flags key information providing assessors with a more complete picture of the educational and social circumstances relevant to the applicant. Some applicants may be set lower offers and some more challenging ones. Interview Post-application interview Successful candidates will be invited to an online interview with an academic (20-30 minutes). The purpose of the interview is for us to find out more about your motivation, analytical thinking, and communication skills. As such, no particular preparation is needed and we do not expect you to demonstrate prior knowledge of economics, finance and/or data science. Our aim, at the meeting, is to identify prospective students who are most likely to enjoy and succeed on the degree.

value.application_deadline_and_schedule: Application deadlines – Wednesday 13 January 2027 at 18.00 (UK time) Selection Assessing your application Admission to Medical Biosciences at Imperial is highly competitive. We use a range of criteria to assess candidates, using your UCAS application. This includes a rigorous review of your educational history and qualifications, your personal statement and your reference. The admissions team will carefully review other key information to gain a complete picture of your circumstances, such as taking into account factors such as your economic, social and educational background. Some applicants may be set lower offers and some more challenging ones. Offers are usually made between January and March. Please be aware that students under the age of 18 will be required to fill in Imperial’s minor policy . Careful consideration is always taken to applicants below the age of 17.

We use a range of criteria to assess candidates, using your UCAS application. This includes a rigorous review of your educational history and qualifications, your personal statement and your reference. The admissions team will carefully review other key information to gain a complete picture of your circumstances, such as taking into account factors such as your economic, social and educational background. Some applicants may be set lower offers and some more challenging ones. Offers are usually made between January and March. Please be aware that students under the age of 18 will be required to fill in Imperial’s minor policy . Careful consideration is always taken to applicants below the age of 17.

course_page_summary.Minimum entry standard: 2:1 (or above) in a Biosciences or Allied Healthcare degree.
course_page_summary.Programme content and career: Four-year graduate MBBS at the University of Cumbria Fusehill Street campus in Carlisle, with placements across North and South Cumbria, medical-science and clinical-skills teaching, a community-based prevention/healthcare-delivery project, clinical placements in years 3–4, pre-foundation assistantship and elective. Graduates obtain an Imperial MBBS primary medical qualification and can apply for UK Foundation Year 1; full GMC registration requires Foundation Year 1 completion and application.
course_page_summary.Accommodation and location: First-year accommodation is guaranteed for applicants who make PCSM their first UCAS choice and submit a University of Cumbria accommodation application by 30 June; years 2–4 subject to availability and application by 30 June. Clinical placements can require travel and/or temporary accommodation.
course_page_summary.Degree subject examples and advice: Published UK subject examples include anatomy, biochemistry, bioengineering, biology, biomedical/healthcare science, cell or molecular biology, clinical sciences, dietetics/nutrition, dentistry, genetics, health and social care, medical sciences, microbiology, midwifery, neuroscience, nursing, physiotherapy, paramedic practice/science, pharmacy, pharmacology, physiology, psychology, public health, radiography, sports science/rehabilitation, occupational therapy/health, and veterinary science/medicine. The list is non-exhaustive; applicants with an unlisted degree or a degree awarded outside the UK are told to contact Cumbria Med Admissions to check suitability.

course_specific_application_materials: Selection Providing that applicants have met (or are predicted to meet) the Academic Requirement, candidates will be ranked and shortlisted for interview according to their Admissions Test scores.
Multiple mini interviews The interviewers are comprised of staff and students with experience in the admissions process, who will contribute to the decision process.

The following criteria may be considered when assessing your application: Undergraduate degree classification GAMSAT/UCAT scores Evidence of commitment to the values of the NHS Constitution Motivation and understanding of medicine as a career Community activities Leadership and teamwork Extracurricular interests Referee’s report Fitness to Practise policy All UK medical schools have a duty to ensure that no member of the public is harmed because of training medical students.
Interview Multiple-Mini interviews (MMIs) may be conducted in a blended format with in person interviews.
Work experience with service-users is strongly recommended and will be assessed during interview, together with other information in the personal statement.

If you have mitigating circumstances at the interview stage, you should inform the PCSM Admissions Officer at the earliest opportunity as these will be reviewed and may be taken into consideration for borderline candidates.

The UCAT You will need to take the University Clinical Aptitude Test (UCAT) to study this course.
Find out more about the UCAT and how to register.
How we use the UCAT The School of Medicine will initially review applications to ensure they meet our minimum academic entry requirements as outlined in our Study pages.
Following receipt of UCAT scores in November, we then begin inviting candidates to attend our Multiple Mini Interviews (MMIs).
Each year, we normally interview the top 1/3 of applicants and will send invitations on a rolling basis from December.
Invitations will explain in detail how the interview will work.
For 2027 entry, all candidates who submitted special circumstances via UCAT will be examined carefully on a case-by-case basis.
We are unable to consider any mitigating circumstances that do not come via UCAT directly.
UCAT scores are used to help decide shortlisting for interview but are not the sole factor.

For 2026 entry, the following UCAT thresholds were applied: UCAT Threshold for Home Applicants SJT: Band 3 minimum (Band 4 discounted) Minimum threshold Total Score: 2320 UCAT Thresholds for Contextual Applicants SJT: Band 3 minimum (Band 4 discounted) Minimum threshold total Score: 2170 All candidates who attend the test are declaring that they are fit to sit the test.
If circumstances occur which might affect performance, candidates must refer to the UCAT Fitness to Test Policy before sitting their test.
On occasion the UCAT Office may communicate significant personal/medical circumstances to the medical school.

The following criteria may be considered when assessing your application: A-level or equivalent predicted (or achieved) grades UCAT scores Referee’s report Personal statement Fitness to Practise policy All UK medical schools have a duty to ensure that no member of the public is harmed as a consequence of training medical students.
Interview If you are shortlisted, you will be invited to take part in Multiple Mini Interviews (MMIs).
The interviews are conducted by a combination of academic staff involved in undergraduate education and experienced healthcare professionals.

The following criteria may be considered when we assess you: evidence of commitment to the values of the NHS Constitution motivation and understanding of medicine as a career empathy work experience and community activities leadership and teamwork Your personal statement may be referred to during the interview stage.
Find out more about our interview process .
Special arrangements for interviews If you are invited to interview, you can request special arrangements to help make sure you can attend.
Please inform us on special adjustments via the survey when you are invited to interview.

Mitigating circumstances If you want us to consider Mitigating Circumstances during the admissions cycle, please refer to the forms below: Mitigating Circumstances Form for MMIs (Deadline 5 working days before your interview) : use this form if you feel you have mitigating circumstances that should be taken into consideration during your Multiple Mini Interviews.
You must state in your UCAS personal statement how you propose to spend your time.
If you wish to make a deferral request in cycle, it is essential that you apply as soon as possible to FEO Admissions Interviews feo-admissions-interviews@imperial.ac.uk .

You must book the test yourself and must only take it once in an admissions cycle. It must be taken in the year that you apply. See the University Clinical Aptitude Test website for registration and test dates. We encourage you to book your test slot at local centre as soon as registration opens. For more information on how we use the UCAT as part of the admissions process, please refer to the entry requirements section of this page. Selection Assessing your application Admission to medicine at Imperial is highly competitive. We use a range of criteria to assess candidates. You must meet the minimum academic requirements and have taken the UCAT admissions test. No offers are made without applicants attending a competitive interview. The following criteria may be considered when assessing your application: A-level or equivalent predicted (or achieved) grades UCAT scores Referee’s report Personal statement Fitness to Practise policy All UK medical schools have a duty to ensure that no member of the public is harmed as a consequence of training medical students. The School of Medicine’s Fitness to Practise policy (PDF) may be activated in cases where significant concerns have been raised about the behaviour of students, including prior to their admission to the School. The interviews are conducted by a combination of academic staff involved in undergraduate education and experienced healthcare professionals. The following criteria may be considered when we assess you: evidence of commitment to the values of the NHS Constitution motivation and understanding of medicine as a career empathy work experience and community activities leadership and teamwork Your personal statement may be referred to during the interview stage. Find out more about our interview process . Special arrangements for interviews If you are invited to interview, you can request special arrangements to help make sure you can attend. published_requirement_or_structure_notes: You will study all these core modules.

Build essential skills in law, programming, and economics as a foundation for advanced study. This module introduces legal and regulatory frameworks, core economic principles, and Python programming, equipping you to analyse the impact of AI on firms, markets and policy. Tailored for diverse backgrounds, it ensures all students are prepared for the challenges ahead.

published_requirement_or_structure_notes: You will take six to seven electives throughout the year depending on the credit value of the modules selected.

Electives will allow you to develop specialist knowledge across rapidly evolving fields such as machine learning, natural language processing, formal methods for safe AI, and domain-specific applications. Each elective will introduce the core analytical models, frameworks, and ethical considerations shaping the modern data-driven landscape.

Deliver a substantial, independent AI project that synthesises your learning across the programme. This capstone module develops your ability to research, design, and implement advanced AI solutions, while demonstrating originality, technical skill, and effective communication through a scholarly report and presentation.

Undertake an internship in industry as an alternative to the Individual Project. Apply programme knowledge in a professional setting, work on a substantial real-world problem and develop independence, analytical skills and effective communication through a final report and presentation, with support from both workplace and academic supervisors.

value.description: Study how AI changes markets and policy through economics, programming, algorithmic regulation and responsible AI. Electives develop specialist interests, followed by an individual project or an industry internship.

published_requirement_or_structure_notes: You’ll study the following core modules.

Using examples from Imperial Enterprise, you will study translation of research from novel ideas, through intellectual property protection, finding the best business partners, to marketable solutions.

You will be supported to source a suitable work-based placement, integrate as part of a team and apply your learning from the taught modules to contribute to the development of a new or existing project. The final work placement-based project will be tailored specifically to this course and your personal interests. For example, you may choose to work in a start-up, or within a tech transfer, science policy or science communications team. This is a chance to showcase how you can put into practice what you've learned throughout the year in a real-world setting.

teaching_and_assessment_methods: Live specialist Lectures and mini lectures
value.description: Connect bioscience with communication, ethical business and entrepreneurship. Study how research becomes a viable innovation, then apply the taught material in a supported work-placement project shaped around your interests.

published_requirement_or_structure_notes: Before the programme begins, you will be expected to complete some pre-study modules which are delivered via Canvas, Imperial Business School’s virtual learning environment (VLE).

These modules will be available to students who have accepted an offer of admission from July onwards, and are designed to give you a basic knowledge of areas which will be covered by the programme throughout the academic year.

published_component_names: Maths and Statistics Foundations for Analytics
published_requirement_or_structure_notes: Core modules rapidly build the theoretical and programming foundations you need for analytics. They are the backbone of the programme and will provide you with a solid combination of tools and knowledge.

published_requirement_or_structure_notes: Each elective will introduce the main analytical models and questions in the area and you will gain expertise in both the language and tools specific to that business area. Real-world data sets and cutting edge tools and models will allow you to apply your knowledge directly within your chosen industry.
You will take six electives from the Business Analytics electives.
You will also have the choice to take one additional elective from a suite of elective modules made available from other Business School MSc programmes.
Over the summer term you will choose to undertake either the Analytics in Business Capstone Project (students take either a Work Placement or Consulting Project) or the Individual Research Report.
Work placement

If you wish to take a longer (four-six month) internship as part of your programme, you can take an extended work placement with the approval of the Academic Director. This is particularly relevant for (but not exclusive to) internships in France, Germany, and other European countries that require students to have student status for the duration of their internships. Please note that additional tuition fees apply.

published_requirement_or_structure_notes: The Imperial Executive MBA electives allow you to specialise in areas of particular interest, developing your expertise with your future career objectives in mind. Our elective options also feature many modules that are offered online, ideal if you have a less flexible work schedule or commute long distances.
You can choose five electives. Electives run in the spring and summer terms of your second year.
Electives are offered in four formats to fit into your schedule:
We also offer a Final Project as an elective, where you’ll work on a real business problem and demonstrate your decision-making and leadership abilities.

The Final Project is a formal report consisting of up to 15,000 words, completed in the second year of the programme. This elective allows you to address a real business problem – you can focus on an issue facing your current employer or an industry of interest.

In order to make an impact on a global scale, you must understand the global environment in which you are working. As an MBA student, you will have opportunities to travel to international destinations to study at partner schools and work with local businesses.

As part of your elective modules, you will complete three immersions developing your knowledge and understanding of deep tech and entrepreneurship ecosystems. These experiences include enhanced ecosystem exposure while bringing industry in the classroom.

The Capstone module takes place in a European tech hub over a five-day period during your second year and provides a practical, immersive opportunity to apply the knowledge, frameworks, and skills developed throughout the programme.
Working intensively in multi-disciplinary teams, you will be required to draw upon your analytical capabilities, strategic thinking, and ability to operate effectively under time pressure.

Global Experience Week takes place during the summer term. It is an unforgettable opportunity that MBA students eagerly anticipate each year. You will learn about the challenges faced by local organisations. You will also explore how a country’s business environment influences their operations.

The optional Global Exchanges programme allows you to increase your international exposure and connect with a global community. You can also build your network by taking advantage of specialised electives at one of our partner schools.

The year-long Executive Leadership Journey will enhance your awareness of your own and other’s strengths. You will work closely with a Careers consultant throughout the programme. Together, you will develop a plan for your future career trajectory. You will also gain insights into yourself and build essential leadership skills.

The third year consists of clinical attachments in hospitals and placements in a primary care setting, supported by structured teaching.

Phase 2 leads to the award of a BSc degree at the end of year four. We have many specialist pathways available, exposing you to research at the cutting edge of the field. You also undertake a supervised research project.

Phase 3 covers the final two years of the MBBS qualification. You rotate through a wide range of clinical specialties, such as obstetrics and gynaecology, psychiatry, general practice and paediatrics.
In the final years, you have the freedom to follow your own interests and undertake an eight-week elective, which you may complete in the UK or overseas.
For full details of each phase, including specific modules, please see the Medicine MBBS/BSc page.
You will initially apply for Medicine MBBS/BSc.
During your fourth or third year of study, you will contact the BSc Programme Officer to apply to undertake an intercalated PhD.

facts.value: PhD/MD(Res) require research, thesis/viva, departmental training, and at least four ECRI skills credits: two by ESA and two more by LSR. They also require plagiarism training and, for entrants from 1 September 2026, Trusted Research e-learning. DACR diagnostic training applies to registrations from 1 September 2025 and is due by ESA. Milestones: ESA by 12 months full-time/24 part-time; LSR by 24/48; progress review by 36/72. A failed progress review may lead to withdrawal or transfer from PhD to MPhil. MPhil requires at least two skills credits and plagiarism training before examination, plus departmental reviews. These are completion/progression requirements, not entry tests. If an academic assessment is passed but skills, plagiarism, or DACR training is incomplete, conditional progression may be allowed subject to a completion deadline agreed with the department, ECRI, or Academic English; missing training does not automatically mean failure. Normal thesis-submission limits: PhD/MD(Res) within 48 months full-time/96 part-time; MPhil within 24/48; internal MBBS intercalated PhD normally within 36/72. Examination-entry forms are due at 44/88 months for PhD/MD(Res) and 20/40 for MPhil. UKRI CDT/DFA handbooks may set their own milestone/submission deadlines. Approved extensions can alter dates. These limits are completion limits, not advertised course durations.

value.application_target: Business (MRes 2YFT), selecting the actual research pathway; Management and Entrepreneurship selects Innovation/Entrepreneurship or Organisational Behaviour/Strategy. This is integrated doctoral entry, not a no-test standalone master.
value.normal_entry: UK upper-second bachelor plus master with Merit/Distinction and a strong dissertation. Exceptionally a strong first-class bachelor without a master may qualify with outstanding references, CV and statement. Quantitative prerequisites include calculus, linear algebra, statistics and data programming. Qualitative Management/Entrepreneurship applicants may join without this background case by case, but still undertake MRes quantitative training.
value.tests: A GMAT or GRE score is compulsory before consideration; no offer is conditional on a later test score. Strong scores are described as approximately the 90th percentile, not guaranteed admission minima. Preferred classic GMAT: 700+ overall, quantitative 50/60, verbal 39/60, writing 6/6, integrated reasoning 8/8. Preferred GMAT Focus: 655+ and component scores around the 90th percentile; valid five years. Preferred GRE: quantitative 165/170, verbal 163/170, analytical writing 5/6. Finance, Economics and Public Policy, and Analytics and Operations prefer GRE; either test is accepted for every pathway.
value.english: Higher English: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with at least 6.5 in each element; TOEFL 100 overall and at least 22 in each element for tests before 21 January 2026, or the new scale at 5.0 overall and 5.0 in each element after transition; or Duolingo 125 overall and at least 115 in each integrated subscore. Validity is two years at course start. Degree exemption requires the degree to have been studied entirely and awarded in a listed country. The Business School list omits Malta, unlike central policy, so do not assume automatic Malta exemption. English may be met after application. Business School wording says “after 21 January” while central guidance says “on or after”; preserve this conflict for a test on the transition date.
value.documents: Submit a CV, statement of purpose, full transcripts, two academic references, the required GMAT/GRE, and English proof. The statement is normally 1–2 A4 pages and should describe research interests and faculty fit. Economics and Public Policy applicants must describe a specific research idea in greater detail. Prior agreement from a willing supervisor is not required.

deadline.required: All supporting documents, references, and the test score are required by the deadline. Incomplete applications are not processed.

value.selection: The Academic Selection Committee shortlists applicants for a faculty panel interview; overseas interviews are online. After the School recommendation, final Registry checks can take up to three weeks.
value.qualification_verification_conflict: The School FAQ requests physical originals for some English qualifications, while the current central offer page says to email accepted qualification proof. Preserve the conflict and follow the actual offer/Registry instruction; do not add an unsupported general postal requirement.

facts.value: The programme begins with a two-year MRes, then a 3–4-year PhD subject to satisfactory progress. Study is full-time with September starts only. Its header says 5–6 years while the FAQ says 4–6; preserve the discrepancy. Part-time/distance study is unavailable and transfers are usually unavailable. Funding includes a Home/Overseas tuition waiver and Graduate Teaching Assistant stipend for up to five years. The published 2026/27 stipend is £29,580 annually, tax-free; a 2027/28 increase is expected but the amount is unpublished. Sixth-year funding may be considered case by case through teaching/research assistant work but is not guaranteed. Continuation depends on satisfactory progress; eligible external awards must be applied for. A President’s PhD award during the MRes may add consumables. No deposit is required. The separate Visiting PhD Scholarship for Black Heritage students supports external PhD students for an initial three-month visit and grants no degree or credits. A supervisor and study plan are agreed and the Director assists admission. No fixed visit deadline is published; 4–6 months’ lead time is recommended, especially for visa applicants. This is an explicit exception to the general FAQ saying visiting applications are not accepted; keep both statements.

facts.value: Normal entry requires one of: an integrated Master’s, at least second class and at least four years; a Bachelor’s, at least second class and at least three years; a taught postgraduate qualification of at least one year; or an approved professional written-examination qualification. Equivalencies, special cases, and qualifying tests may apply. The four-year EngD combines mainly industry-based research, academic/industrial supervisors, and taught/professional components. The year-one report is at most 10,000 words with an oral assessment. One reassessment is allowed; an MPhil in Quantitative Non-Destructive Evaluation may be an exit award if requirements are met. A PhD registrant may transfer to EngD within 12 months, subject to conditions, and complete taught elements within 36 rather than 24 months. Research reports recur every six months. All required modules must be completed, normally with only one reassessment per failed module; two technical optional courses and professional-skills courses are required. Year-one assessment may require remedial action or withdrawal. The final thesis is normally due by the four-year programme end or within one additional calendar year, and must demonstrate industrial context. Regulations alone establish no current recruitment target, date, or fee amount.

facts.value: The DSc is a higher doctorate for published work showing exceptional original research and sustained international distinction. Eligible applicants hold an Imperial/merged-institution degree (including University of London degrees awarded through Imperial) or are Imperial academic staff with at least two years’ service. Submit the Registry Assessment Records form, prescribed fee, CV, numbered chronological publication list, a 10–12 A4-page contribution statement, and electronic copies of the work (normally the 20 most significant items). Work should normally be in English; an approved translation may be accepted by exception. Verify contributions to joint work and identify work previously used for a degree. Concurrent application elsewhere for a comparable award is barred. The committee conducts faculty vetting and then obtains three external referees. Part of the fee may be refunded if the application cannot proceed. One further submission after failure is normally permitted; further resubmission needs Senate discretion and uses the regulations then in force. Appeals are limited to procedural irregularity. Successful work is deposited in Spiral. The regulations publish no fee amount or annual deadline. This is not a taught course or ordinary PhD intake.

facts.value: The successful four-year award covers UKRI Home tuition. The quoted foundation-year stipend is GBP 21,805 plus GBP 2,000 London weighting for 2026/27; years two to four add GBP 26,500 per year. During PhD years, the supervisor receives GBP 5,000 annually for research training; conference support is GBP 300 per year and supplementary activities are conditional. The grant covers Home-level tuition only: the registering PhD department must cover the Overseas-fee difference or the applicant must secure it, which may limit department choice. Separate foundation and PhD visa applications are required and their costs are not covered. Foundation pathways are Biomedical Research MRes, Innovation/Entrepreneurship PGCert, or Computational Biomedicine PGCert; each includes two rotations. PhD registration in year two is separate. facts.value: For October 2027, five EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Awards are listed for applicants meeting UK residency criteria. They cover Home fees, the stated current £23,805 annual stipend, and £1,000 travel/equipment over 3.5 years. Expected preparation is a first-class MEng or first-class Bachelor’s plus a distinction-level Master’s. Eligible applicants are ranked after acceptance by the relevant department/College round; no separate scholarship form is used, and an earlier departmental deadline overrides the central nomination deadline. Up to four Doctoral Teaching Scholarships are listed for 2027/28, covering full Home/Overseas fees and about £31,380 annually for 4.5 years, with annual review; at least one is for an Overseas applicant. Teaching totals about 15 full-time-equivalent months across the award. Applicants first need a PhD offer naming a supervisor, then contact the coordinator, submit a teaching statement, and interview. Suggested 15 February/15 April dates have no stated year. QRT Labs lists more than 20 fully funded awards across Computing, Mathematics, and Business; these are not automatic for every applicant. AI4Health is normally Home-fee-only and may require conference approval; do not assume Overseas fees are funded. Direct CSC applications outside Imperial’s scheme have no guaranteed departmental fee contribution.

facts.value: Two central staff-fee schemes apply. Tuition Fee Remission is for substantive Imperial/wholly-owned-company staff; Honorary staff, directly externally funded staff, NHS employees, and relatives are excluded. It covers postgraduate degrees, including certificates/diplomas but not CPD, and requires 12 months’ service before study, an employment contract covering the entire expected degree, approved business case, and a normal competitive course offer with all conditions met. The discount is two-thirds of the Home fee, prorated to employment FTE; the balance remains payable and excess awards reduce remission. Staff-student fees apply to full-time project Research Assistants/Clinical Research Fellows undertaking doctoral programmes, including integrated routes. There is no 12-month service requirement, but the employment must start by the degree and cover its full duration, and grant-administration conditions must be met. The fee is one-third of the Home rate regardless of fee status. If employment ends, fees are recalculated. Resignation during study or within 12 months after completion requires full repayment; resignation 12–24 months after completion requires 50%. Redundancy, involuntary termination, and scheduled end of fixed-term contract are exceptions. Older departmental three-year rules do not override the current whole-duration contract rule.

The PhD builds on the MRes project and includes BBC science communication, responsible research, human-centred design, policy, hackathons, EVOLVE placements, and optional InnovaLAB start-ups. value.transition: Near the end of the foundation year, develop a PhD proposal with prospective supervisors. It should align with the MRC remit; interdisciplinary work on diagnosis, treatment, or prevention is welcome.
value.phd: The PhD project lasts three years and includes ECRI, faculty, and HealthBRIDGE training. Early-stage review is typically within nine months; late-stage review is at 18–24 months of the PhD project, followed by thesis/viva.
value.support: Students receive six-monthly development reviews and a wellbeing action plan, along with cohort workshops/retreats. The source describes a charity-related project partnership, optional collaborative work placement, and conditional MRC supplement/training support; placements and supplements are not guaranteed.

value.structure: The programme starts with a two-year MRes; successful completion controls progression to the PhD. Year one provides compulsory/recommended theory and research-methods training by pathway. Year two selects field modules and completes a research project. Published module lists are examples and may change.

Management and Entrepreneurship, year on: Introduction to the Practice of Research

value.elective_scope: Separate published pathway lists include economics/finance, qualitative and quantitative methods, marketing, optimisation and machine learning; not every elective is required or available in every pathway.
value.mres_project: Second year: title/outline in early October, progress report in early March, dissertation in summer term followed by oral examination; contributes to overall MRes mark.
value.phd: Students choose primary and secondary supervisors and complete supervisor-guided specialist training and research seminars. The Early Stage Assessment in PhD year one is a written paper and presentation; Late Stage Review occurs in year two. Thesis research, conferences, and academic job-market support follow. The final Continuing Research Stage ends with a viva; dates/requirements follow the programme’s current handbook.

facts.value: The 2026/27 PhD/MPhil/MD(Res) regulations normally bar re-admission in the same or closely related field after prior Imperial research withdrawal, including advanced standing. Concurrent degree registration normally needs Senate-approved arrangements. Direct MPhil students may transfer to PhD after at least12 full-time or24 part-time months via written report and oral examination; one further attempt is permitted within six months. Transfers between PhD and MD(Res) are conditional on degree-specific eligibility and cannot occur after examination entry. Changing full-time/part-time status needs supervisor and departmental approval. These are registration/progression rules; no direct MPhil application availability is inferred.
